Specific finding: Joint interventions on profession-position representation neurons can produce gender-edit indirect effects far larger than the sum of effects from intervening on those neurons individually. The paper directly compared summed individual indirect effects with simultaneous all-neuron interventions. NIE-sum versus NIE-all was 6.8 versus 130.9 for GPT2-distil, 4.0 versus 112.3 for small, 3.5 versus 116.0 for medium, 2.1 versus 96.9 for large, and 2.9 versus 225.2 for xl. These are effect-metric values, not percentages. The all-neuron intervention equals the total effect by construction.

Specific finding: GPT-2 Small IOI circuits can achieve high normalized task-score faithfulness and preserve nearly all correct choices while reproducing only a small fraction of the full model's errors. On a scored sample containing all 884 errors from a 100,000-prompt IOI census and 10,000 sampled correct prompts, with sampling weights, mean-ablated circuits achieve 97.3–99.5% correct agreement but 11.4–41.7% exact-error agreement. The manual circuit has normalized faithfulness F=0.956, 99.5% correct agreement, and 15.2% error agreement. Gap intervals use 10,000 stratified bootstrap draws; Edge Pruning averages three fitted seeds, with uncertainty conditional on fitted masks.
Specific finding: Increasing model-error weight or distinct-error exposure during IOI ACDC discovery can improve exact-error reproduction while reducing correct-case agreement. Assigning existing errors 50% of discovery KL weight raises error agreement from 9.3% to 37.0% while correct agreement falls from 98.7% to 91.0%. Using 500 distinct errors and 500 correct discovery examples raises error agreement to 44.2% and lowers correct agreement to 91.4%. Enrichment changes discovery composition as well as prevalence; detailed uncertainty and repeated-run results are not supplied.
Specific finding: Restoring selected omitted head–position outputs can substantially improve an IOI reference circuit's exact-error reproduction with a small, sample-dependent loss of correct agreement, beyond reported matched random extensions and a scalar subject-bias control. Gradient screening followed by exact binary interventions selects 63 added rules from 3,574 supported additions, using separate training and validation sets. On a frozen 26,000-prompt test set with 225 errors and 25,775 correct predictions, error agreement rises from 14.22% to 75.11%, while correct agreement falls from 99.34% to 98.93%. The net changes are 137 additional error agreements and 106 fewer correct agreements. Reported structurally matched random extensions reach 17.33–41.33% error agreement; a validation-fitted subject-bias control reaches 20.44% at approximately matched correct agreement. Under resampling, error agreement rises from 40.89% to 60.89% and correct agreement from 91.41% to 97.67%. Table 4 additionally summarizes a fresh 5,200-prompt check with a 0.85-point correct-agreement loss, exceeding the original 0.5-point tolerance; detailed methods for that check and the random-control panel are not supplied.

Specific finding: On selected stereotyped coreference errors, smaller extracted circuits can produce the correct answer while larger circuits increasingly reproduce the full model's biased answer. Appendix F.1.2 reports nonmonotonic soft-faithfulness curves and separately tracks correct and biased top predictions. Near the initial soft-faithfulness drop, circuits often predict the correct profession despite selection for full-model errors. Increasing circuit size subsequently raises biased-answer rates, particularly with positional differentiation. No exact correction rate or component-level mediation analysis is supplied in the accessible text.
location: Appendix F.1.2; Figure 11 and its caption

experiment_summary: Specific finding: A one-dimensional direction in GPT-2 Small's final-token residual stream can transfer IOI name-position effects through downstream name-mover and backup-name-mover heads. A one-dimensional DAS direction flips predictions approximately 80% of the time on a test set using different templates and names. A separately constructed position-conditioned mean-difference direction has approximately 0.85 cosine similarity with it, with a smaller patching effect. Path patching finds that the intervention acts largely through name-mover and backup-name-mover heads, with attribution scores close to those without intervention. S-inhibition's upstream role is adopted from the cited IOI analysis rather than newly demonstrated here.
location: Real-world case study: the IOI task; Distributed alignment search

experiment_summary: Specific finding: Selected rank-one components of GPT-2 Small inhibition heads carry positional signals that causally affect downstream name selection. Removing the highest-composing component generally reduces the attention-based inhibition score by a reported 7–14%, with head 7.3 a weak-effect exception. Replacing head outputs with scaled component directions switches positional attention on 200 name-order-balanced IOI prompts, unlike the reported random-head and other-component controls. Channel interchange between minimally different prompts yields 97.5% fractional logit-difference decrease and 35% interchange accuracy. Comparison values from Makelov et al. are cited prior results, not experiments rerun here.

Specific finding: IOI prompts differing in the order of their first two names can recruit distinct feature-level pathways even when their important attention heads occupy similar functional roles. Hierarchical Attribution and QK analysis recover name-mover, S-inhibition, induction, and previous-token head roles in two examples. The paper interprets the after-and answer through consecutive-entity and consecutive-entity-association features, and the before-and answer through centered-entity features with suppression of the consecutive-entity pathway. The authors describe the account as non-rigorous; no feature-intervention validation or broader name-order evaluation is reported.

Specific finding: GPT-2 Small's name-mover head (9,9) can retain its IOI output role while receiving substantially different incoming signals in ABBA and BABA prompt representatives. Representative comparisons report negative destination-signal cosine similarity and near-zero source-signal similarity for head (9,9). Gemini 3 Flash interpretations characterize BABA paths as identifying the second element of a parallel pair, while ABBA paths use broader structural-completion and parallel-structure descriptions. Claude assisted reduction of annotated traces into qualitative figures. These observations establish differences in selected signal summaries more directly than the correctness of their semantic labels.
location: Section 3.1, Figures 4–5; Appendix F.2–F.3; Appendix H.3–H.4

experiment_summary:
Specific finding: Within a selected GPT-2 Small IOI pathway, interpreted SAE feature-pair contributions raise the pre-softmax attention score to the indirect object on BABA templates and lower the score to the subject on ABBA templates. Decompose the selected name-mover QK pathway into attention-output SAE features on the query side and residual-stream SAE features on the key side. The analyzed feature-pair contributions are positive for the Name2 score on BABA prompts, where Name2 is IO, and negative on ABBA prompts, where Name2 is S. Eight interpreted pairs explain 62% of score variance across 100 prompts; entries involving at least one reconstruction-error term explain approximately 15%. This is a measured pathway-score decomposition, without an independent behavioral necessity test of all eight pairs or a demonstration of their isolated effect on softmax-normalized attention.
Specific finding: In GPT-2 Small's tested IOI prompts, induction-layer positional information substantially depends on whether the repeated name originally occurred before or after the conjunction ' and'. Keeping the SAE reconstruction error, individually zero-ablate layer-5 features at S2 and identify three with average logit-difference decreases greater than 0.2. Path patching into S-inhibition-head values localizes the same three features, interpreted as duplicate tokens before or after ' and'. Independent noising replaces layers 5 and 6 attention outputs at S2: donor prompts changing names, absolute positions, and subject separation while preserving conjunction-relative order recover 93% of average logit difference, normalized relative to zero ablation. Changing only ' and' to ' alongside' recovers approximately 43% (0.436 in Table 4); tested replacements range from 0.289 to 0.678. These comparisons support conjunction dependence without proving that all other positional information is absent.

Specific finding: Within a selected GPT-2 Small IOI pathway, interpreted SAE feature-pair contributions raise the pre-softmax attention score to the indirect object on BABA templates and lower the score to the subject on ABBA templates. Expanded the selected pathway using layer-5 attention features and layer-9 residual features. Four interpreted query-side features and two key-side features formed eight pairs explaining 62% of score variance across 100 prompts. Terms containing at least one reconstruction error explained approximately 15%; SAE biases were excluded. The interpreted pairs gave positive contributions on BABA prompts and negative contributions on ABBA prompts, motivating partial IO-boosting versus S-inhibition interpretations. No independent feature-pair intervention establishes complete mediation.
Specific finding: In GPT-2 Small's tested IOI prompts, induction-layer positional information substantially depends on whether the repeated name originally occurred before or after the conjunction ' and'. Jointly replaced layers 5–6 attention outputs at S2 using counterfactual prompts with randomized names, prepended filler, and additional filler between subject occurrences, while preserving name order relative to “ and”. The authors report approximately 93% average logit-difference recovery relative to zero ablation. Replacing only “ and” with “ alongside” yielded approximately 43% recovery under the same reference. A footnote reports similar effects for five additional alternatives, but their appendix details are unavailable. These tests favor conjunction-sensitive positional information over the tested absolute-position, distance, and conjunction-independent alternatives without proving sole dependence.
location: Applying SAEs to QK circuits: S-Inhibition Heads Sometimes Do IO-Boosting

experiment_summary:
Specific finding: For gender-swapped Winobias continuations, the natural indirect effect through all attention-head mediators exceeds the corresponding natural direct effect in GPT-2-small, medium, large, and xl. Figure 8 compares concurrent all-head natural direct and indirect effects across five GPT-2 variants. The indirect effect is larger in every variant except distil. This comparison concerns the chosen attention-weight mediators and does not establish that attention stores most gender information or that all other pathways are negligible.
Specific finding: A small subset of attention heads can match the joint indirect effect of intervening on all attention heads for gender-swapped coreference continuations in autoregressive language models. Individual and joint attention-weight replacements were evaluated using Top-k and greedy head selection. On GPT-2-small's filtered Winobias development subset, containing 87 of 160 format-compatible examples, 10 of 144 heads matched the all-head indirect effect; the first six selected heads were in layers 4 and 5. Appendix D reports saturation using approximately 4–5% of heads on Winogender and 6–8% on Winobias across distil/small/medium/large. Transformer-XL and XLNet-base Winobias heatmaps additionally showed sparse effects. These results concern matching an aggregate intervention effect, not complete circuit recovery or held-out generalization.
Specific finding: A small fraction of profession-position representation coordinates can match the joint all-coordinate gender-edit effect in GPT-2, with influential coordinates disproportionately concentrated in embeddings and early hidden layers. The paper compared layerwise top-5% coordinate interventions and cumulative Top-k subsets, adding neurons in batches of 96. In GPT-2-small, approximately 4% of candidate neurons matched the all-neuron intervention effect; 57% of selected neurons came from the embedding and first hidden layer. GPT-2 variants showed strong early-layer effects. Gender-neutral interventions and additional architectures did not reproduce the same depth profile.
location: Section 5.4, Attention heads mediate most of the effect; Figure 8

experiment_summary:
Specific finding: Larger GPT-2 variants tend to exhibit larger gender-swap total effects on adapted Winobias and Winogender, although the relationship is not strictly monotonic. Filtered Winobias development total effects for distil/small/medium/large/xl were 0.118/0.249/0.774/0.751/1.049, with respective retained counts of 61/87/99/94/101 out of 160 format-compatible examples. Filtered Winogender BLS effects were 0.081/0.103/0.322/0.364/0.342, retaining 15/21/23/24/25 of 44 examples. Filtering removes negative effects and the bottom quartile of positive effects, so these comparisons use different selected examples. Unfiltered comparisons also showed an overall size trend with reversals. Professions effects were not well correlated with size.
Specific finding: Trained GPT-2 variants can exhibit substantially larger occupation- and pronoun-edit total effects than a randomly initialized GPT-2-small model on candidate-probability gender evaluations. Table 1 reports total effects of 0.066 on Winobias, 0.045 on Winogender, and 0.117 on Professions for random GPT-2-small, compared with 0.249, 0.103, and 112.275 for trained GPT-2-small. The other trained GPT-2 variants also exceed this random control on these metrics. Attention heatmaps additionally lack the trained models' localization pattern in the random model. This does not isolate which training examples or objectives produced the differences.

Specific finding: Selected attribution-ranked SAE ablations can reduce gender–profession distributional skew while retaining or slightly improving name-based gender accuracy in Demo-R prompts. Table C.6 reports that Gemma-2-9B-IT Gender-Name attribution ablation changes name accuracy from 0.873 to 0.880 and profession KL from 0.686 to 0.644. Gender-Profession attribution ablation retains accuracy at 0.873 and reduces KL to 0.662. Appendix G.1 reports corresponding 2B gender-KL reductions of 24.0% and 23.6%, with small recognition gains. No uncertainty estimates or independent feature-selection/evaluation split are specified. The observed non-overlap Gender-Name condition has slightly lower KL and higher accuracy than full attribution, so full attribution is not uniquely best in Table C.6.
Specific finding: Ablating gender–profession SAE features selected from structured association tasks can improve Winogender coreference accuracy, including stereotype-conflicting gotcha cases. Table E.9 reports baseline overall/gotcha accuracy of 0.785/0.696 versus 0.814/0.796 for attribution ablation. Correlation, intersection, and non-overlap also improve both metrics; attribution has the highest observed overall and gotcha scores. No uncertainty estimates establish significance of differences between methods. The transfer test demonstrates utility on this coreference benchmark without isolating a unique stereotype-specific mechanism.

Specific finding: Among selected strongly gender-biased GPT-2 Small prompts, higher-NDF circuits can identify gender-associated SAE feature sets whose ablation produces larger measured bias reductions than sets identified from lower-NDF circuits. Of 986 prompts, 50 have stereotypical-minus-antistereotypical probability greater than 0.5; 32 additionally have a best-of-ten circuit with NDF above 0.8. Zeroing identified gender features yields reported mean absolute logit-bias reductions of 0.810 versus 0.234 and probability-bias reductions of 0.063 versus 0.011 for best versus worst circuits. All four paired outcome comparisons report one-sided Wilcoxon p<0.0001 and Rosenthal r=0.737–0.836. An unpaired analysis uses one original-query circuit for each of all 50 prompts, split into 27 high-NDF and 23 low-NDF examples. It reports probability-bias reductions of 0.066 versus 0.038 and logit-bias reductions of 0.912 versus 0.320. The groups already differ in initial logit bias, and the paired analysis conditions on successful best-circuit recovery. Feature-selection details and individual-attention-head SAE localization remain limited.
location: Section 6.5; Table 2; Appendix C.13 and Table A7; Appendix C.13.1

experiment_summary:
Specific finding: Residual-stream patches sourced from demographic statements can change OLMo-7B-Instruct depression-risk judgments on otherwise shared hospital-course inputs, with higher positive prediction rates under female and Black donor conditions. For gender comparisons, the authors replace gendered terms in selected BHCs to construct gender-neutral inputs; race comparisons use the selected BHC set. Source demographic-token residual activations are patched into the final target-prompt token, using layer 18 for gender and layer 20 for race, both at scaling factor 2. Settings are selected using 100 BHCs. Over 1,000 evaluation courses and four prompts, female-minus-male positive-risk rates average 3.50 ± 2.2 percentage points and Black-minus-white rates average 8.25 ± 5.8 points. The text does not define the ± quantities. On the two prompts requesting demographic disclosure, strict assignment fractions are 0.96 female, 0.94 male, 0.79 Black, and 0.76 white; relaxed assignment is 1.00 but counts outputs omitting demographics as successful. Risk labels are parsed from Yes/No or validation-derived substrings. Gold clinical risk accuracy is not evaluated. A separate explicit-prompt comparison reports gaps of 3.6 and 4.3 percentage points for gender and race, respectively.
Specific finding: Replacing a condition-token MLP activation with a male-statement donor activation can substantially increase male-patient generation in selected clinical vignette tasks. The study selects sites using normalized demographic-token probability increases and evaluates vignette generation at temperature 0.7, with 1,000 samples per condition. OLMo-7B layer-18 patches scaled by at least 2 yield male fractions of 1.00 for multiple sclerosis and sarcoidosis. Scaled Llama layer-5 patches also yield 1.00 for both. Table 3 reports Gemma layer-16 fractions of 0.83/0.92 without scaling and 0.85/0.92 with scaling, despite prose describing scaling as ineffective. OLMo-32B layer-39 patches yield 0.96 for multiple sclerosis without a scaling benefit; sarcoidosis was excluded because females were not overrepresented. These results establish control through whole-vector replacement, not exclusive localization of a naturally used demographic mechanism.
Specific finding: MLP activations elicited by sex-associated medical conditions can redirect gendered generation in other clinical conditions and selected profession-completion prompts. Using the Section 2.2 setup at layer 18, scaled prostate-token donor patches produce male clinical vignettes in all reported evaluated samples. Preeclampsia donor patches increase the female fraction for colon-cancer vignettes from 0.08 to 0.96 without scaling and 1.00 at scaling factor 2. For profession transfer, 17 templates crossed with 28 female-associated professions yield 46 selected female-pronoun sentences. Twenty select scaling factor 5; patches flip 25 of the remaining 26 sentences. Increasing scaling to 7 also flips the final sentence, constituting an additional adjustment after inspecting that failure. The transfer result concerns these selected completions rather than general cross-domain demographic control.
Specific finding: F1 agreement between a feature's positive-activation support and a simple task-attribute predicate provides a useful proxy for that feature's task-specific interpretability.

Specific finding: SAE features selected by agreement with IOI attribute predicates can capture substantial task-relevant intervention effects and guide useful attribute editing. Keeping or deleting task-SAE features with interpretation F1 at least 0.6 often preserved or disrupted substantial IOI performance. Attribute editing guided by F1 rankings performed close to interpretation-agnostic greedy editing. Additional counterfactual feature-patching tests at name-mover outputs found strong coverage at threshold 0.6, while higher thresholds reduced counterfactual transfer. Fixing a subset above F1 0.8 could still retain the base prediction when other features were patched. The text does not establish independent held-out evaluation of all interpretation-selection choices.
location: Section 5.2, Test 3; Figure 4; Appendices A.12–A.13 and A.16; Figures 28–31

experiment_summary:
Specific finding: Classifiers can assign negligible attention to sensitive or task-diagnostic tokens while achieving substantially higher accuracy than comparison models trained with those tokens removed or anonymized. On SST+Wikipedia, worst-head-penalized BERT at λ=1 achieves 90.2% accuracy versus 90.8% without manipulation and 50.4% with review tokens removed, while its maximum-head attention-mass statistic falls from 96.2% to below 0.001%. Manipulated BiLSTM pronoun-based gender identification retains 100% accuracy with attention mass below 10^-6%, compared with 63.3% for its token-removal/anonymization control. Smaller SST models lose substantial accuracy under manipulation.
Specific finding: Suppressing attention on gender indicators can make human observers judge occupation predictions as uninfluenced by gender while assigning the explanations trust ratings near those of original attention. The study compares original dot-product attention, a trained Wiegreffe–Pinter adversarial-attention comparator, and the proposed manipulation. The reported gender-influence rate is 66% with original attention and 0% under either manipulated scheme. Mean trust ratings are 3.00, 1.00, and 2.67 out of 4, respectively. Each participant supplies one trust rating after viewing each scheme's 50 examples. Classifiers achieve roughly 96% accuracy, and reported Fleiss' κ is 0.97. The study has only three participants and supplies no inferential significance test.
models_studied: ["Embedding + dot-product attention classifier", "Single-layer BiLSTM + dot-product attention classifier", "BERT-base with restricted self-attention"]

experiment_summary:
Specific finding: ReLU sparse autoencoders trained on two-dimensional representations of four composed generating features can prefer dictionaries of feature combinations over dictionaries aligned with the generating features across a broad tested hyperparameter grid. Compared five SAE realizations per setting across five learning rates from 0.00003 to 0.003 and five L1 coefficients from 0.01 to 1, training each on 128 million samples. The comparisons display lowest-loss and highest-monosemanticity realizations, using the cited Engineering Monosemanticity measure. Composed dictionaries predominate. Identical amplitudes allow a mostly monosemantic realization at learning rate 0.0003 and lambda 0.01. Independent amplitudes yield more consistently composed solutions; occasional monosemantic realizations have higher loss than composed alternatives. Exact grid-wide recovery counts are not supplied.
Specific finding: Including isolated generating features in most training inputs does not ensure that a sparse autoencoder recovers those features individually rather than their combinations. Tested one-hot mixture probabilities of 0.5 and 0.75, displaying results for 0.75. In the displayed distribution, each isolated-feature configuration has probability 0.1875 and each composed configuration probability 0.0625. More lowest-loss SAEs recover primitive directions than in the exclusively composed setting, but recovery remains unreliable and no robust learning-rate or L1-coefficient trend is reported. Exact recovery counts are unavailable in the supplied prose.
models_studied: ["ReLU SAEs on four-input, two-hidden-dimensional ReLU-output toy models"]
location: Results — Correlated Feature Amplitudes; Uncorrelated Feature Amplitudes

experiment_summary: Specific finding: Replacing two additive Boolean features with mutually exclusive conjunction and exclusive-case features reduces expected active-feature count when the features coactivate, but can increase the sum of their marginal coding entropies. Analytical coding calculation: the two-feature expected L0 is p_A+p_B, whereas the three mutually exclusive features have expected L0 p_A+p_B−p_AB. Applying the paper's featurewise entropy rule gives costs H(p_A)+H(p_B) and H(p_A−p_AB)+H(p_B−p_AB)+H(p_AB). These expressions permit different preferences from L0 minimization; the text discusses the equal-marginal case as correlation varies. This is a derivation for stipulated Boolean representations, not a trained-SAE experiment.

Specific finding: When a child feature implies a parent feature, SAE sparsity objectives can favor encoding the parent direction inside the child latent and suppressing the parent latent on child examples. Four-feature toy SAEs recover independent directions but absorb parent features after hierarchical co-occurrence is introduced. Appendix A.2 constructs exact reconstructions with expected L1 cost p11(2-delta)+p10, decreasing with absorption. Further toys show partial absorption under magnitude variation and imperfect co-occurrence.

Specific finding: A wider sparse dictionary can isolate a topic-specific feature where a narrower dictionary's closest feature has a broader interpretation. Inspects 36 decoder-neighbor features selected around one historical-event feature across 8× vanilla, 8× TopK, and 32× TopK dictionaries, using UMAP and GPT-4o descriptions of top activations. Identifies a Brexit-specific wider-dictionary feature whose closest narrower counterpart is described as Historical Movements. This qualitative contrast does not rule out composition of narrower features or establish complete topic exclusivity.

Specific finding: SAE splitting of binary IOI position information into many narrower features can recur above chance across training seeds and datasets. Observed position information split across ten or more features with small, mostly non-overlapping supports and no clear semantic interpretation. Comparisons across seeds on the same dataset and across different datasets found feature similarity above chance. The supplied text does not give the comparison metric, numerical similarities, sample counts, or uncertainty.

Specific finding: Meta-SAE decompositions can describe selected SAE feature splits as retention of a shared component together with addition of more specific contextual components. Trained a separate meta-SAE jointly on eight decoder dictionaries and identified splits using cosine similarity above 0.7. A broad talk-related latent and its listed descendants share a talking/speaking meta-latent, with additional noun, imperative, participial, and contextual components. Smaller dictionaries reportedly activate fewer meta-latents on average. The source claims seven descendants but lists six; unequal recurrence across dictionary sizes may influence the learned decomposition.
location: Using Meta-SAEs to Interpret Split Features; footnote 1

experiment_summary:
Specific finding: Increasing ConSDL dictionary width together with its active-atom budget can produce multiple distinct, related atoms corresponding to a broader atom in a smaller dictionary. Across four backbones, 45–55% of consistency-qualified 4-fold ConSDL atoms have at least two qualified counterparts at 16-fold expansion, compared with 12–37% for ReLU and lower reported fractions for TopK. Selected retriever and plant examples have differing activation patterns and more specific descriptive labels. The selected retriever example uses counterpart similarities of 0.65–0.75, differing from the population analysis's threshold. The evidence establishes geometric correspondence and selected semantic distinctions rather than a general ground-truth granularity result.
Specific finding: Multiple ConSDL atoms can correspond geometrically to a single baseline SAE atom while exhibiting distinct, related activation patterns. The source describes five ConSDL counterparts to a ReLU beer-bottle atom, with image-level activation Jaccard overlaps 0.36–0.57, and seven counterparts to a ReLU baseball atom, with token-level overlaps 0.06–0.28. The language labels are assigned by Claude Opus 5.5 from top-activating contexts. Across backbones, one-to-many correspondence is more frequent from consistent ReLU atoms to ConSDL than in reverse, using cross-seed consistency and decoder-similarity thresholds of at least 0.7. These findings support selected distinctions and geometric asymmetry rather than dictionary-wide proof of finer semantic features.
location: Section 6.1; Figures 6 and 12; Appendix E.2; Figure 15

experiment_summary: Specific finding: Increasing the dictionary width of standard non-hierarchical SAEs can degrade downstream feature-quality evaluation scores. The executed width sweep reports deteriorating downstream feature-quality metrics for alternative SAE architectures, contrasting with generally stable or improving Matryoshka results. The supplied prose does not enumerate all architecture-by-metric outcomes, so this supports an existential degradation claim rather than a universal scaling law or a conjunction with improved individual-feature interpretability.

Specific finding: Feature splitting can explain why wider non-hierarchical SAEs exhibit poorer concept isolation, while hierarchical dictionaries preserve useful abstraction levels. Inverse SCR scaling persists across intervention budgets, weakening a simple fixed-budget explanation, but feature splitting is not directly manipulated or established as the cause.

Specific finding: SAEs trained on language-model activations can exhibit causally consequential feature absorption across JumpReLU, L1-regularized, and TopK architectures. A probe-alignment and dominant-ablation detector finds absorption in every tested SAE, including hundreds of Gemma Scope SAEs and smaller L1/TopK suites. For Gemma layer 3, latent 1085 carries spelling information absent from main latent 6510 on '_short'; removing its probe component eliminates its substantial ablation effect.
Specific finding: Increasing SAE dictionary width or reducing the number of active latents can increase feature absorption rather than eliminate it. Measured absorption rates rise with larger width and lower L0 across Gemma Scope SAEs. The detector omits partial and distributed absorption, and trends vary by letter.

Specific finding: Changing nested reconstruction-loss weights or the number of nested dictionaries can trade Matryoshka SAE replacement fidelity against absorption and concept-isolation scores. Weighting prefix losses by the number of added latents improved replacement cross-entropy relative to equal weighting but worsened absorption and SCR. Three groups improved loss recovered relative to five while worsening absorption and SCR; ten groups slightly improved absorption but worsened loss recovered and automated interpretability. The group-count comparison also changes prefix layouts, so it does not isolate group count independently of layout.
location: Appendices G.1 and G.3; Figures 16 and 18

experiment_summary:
Specific finding: Adjusting an inner Matryoshka reconstruction-loss weight can approximately cancel opposing hedging and absorption distortions in a hierarchical parent latent. A Matryoshka SAE is trained on 100M synthetic samples. The parent fires with probability 0.25, and each child fires conditionally with probability 0.15. Strong inner-prefix influence produces positive child mixing, while zero inner weight produces absorption. With outer weight one, an inner weight of 0.25 yields a near-correct representation according to the reported encoder/decoder cosine patterns.
Specific finding: A shared Matryoshka prefix-loss weight can leave simultaneous residual hedging and absorption when child features have unequal firing probabilities. Appendix A.8 changes the hierarchical toy's child probabilities and manually selects an inner weight near 0.17. The text reports slight hedging of feature 4 and slight absorption of feature 2 in the parent latent. This is a finite manual balancing result, without an exhaustive coefficient search or impossibility proof.
models_studied: ["Four-latent Matryoshka SAE on four orthogonal hierarchical features"]

experiment_summary:
Specific finding: Training sparse autoencoders with low-rank polynomial decoders can improve mean single-feature semantic-classification F1 over corresponding linear-decoder baselines. Table 1 compares TopK, BatchTopK, and Matryoshka with polynomial counterparts using logistic regression on the feature selected by largest class-mean activation difference. Reported mean F1 increases in all 12 comparisons, ranging from 0.7 to 12.3 percentage points, approximately 8.3 points averaged across configurations. Repeated-seed uncertainty is not reported.
Specific finding: Polynomial sparse decoders can improve single-feature probing while retaining cross-entropy recovery close to corresponding linear sparse decoders. Table 1 reports absolute cross-entropy-recovery differences no larger than 0.003 between polynomial and corresponding vanilla dictionaries. MSE is similar in scale but sometimes higher for PolySAE. No equivalence test or uncertainty estimates are supplied.
Specific finding: Orthonormalizing a shared low-rank polynomial decoder projection can improve semantic probing F1 without increasing its parameter count. Adding orthogonality to the low-rank variant raises F1 from 75.0 to 77.9 while MSE changes from 0.53 to 0.55 and the reported parameter count remains 13.3M. Earlier factorization reduces the table's parameter count from 37.7M to 13.3M and F1 from 76.0 to 75.0. These parameter counts conflict with the stated full-width formula; the final variant exceeds the initial polynomial variant by 1.9 F1 points.
Specific finding: Polynomial-decoder SAE training can increase Wasserstein distances between class-conditional latent activation distributions relative to corresponding linear-decoder training. Table 1 reports larger class-conditional 1-Wasserstein distances for polynomial variants in all displayed comparisons. The authors summarize increases as approximately 2–10-fold; some rounded entries imply ratios exceeding ten. The text does not establish normalization excluding latent-scale changes as a contributor.

Specific finding: Sums of first-order decoder directions selected from a polynomial SAE can improve compositional target-token ranks more than corresponding vanilla-SAE direction sums on authored prompts. The intervention adds alpha times the sum of two first-order decoder directions at every token during 50-token greedy generation. Target-token rank improves over no steering in 230/324 prompt–concept pairs, with three degradations. Concept-level aggregates improve over no steering in 27/27 concepts and over vanilla SAE in 21/27, with reported mean rank improvement of 41.5 against vanilla. Coefficient selection, direction normalization, baseline feature correspondence, and the exact rank-measurement procedure are insufficiently specified.
Specific finding: Selected polynomial-SAE first-order direction sums can align more closely with supervised compositional-concept mean-difference directions than corresponding vanilla-SAE sums. Cosine similarity to normalized layer-8 positive-minus-negative activation means averages 0.372±0.093 for PolySAE versus 0.311±0.158 for vanilla SAE. The paper reports 11 PolySAE wins, two vanilla wins, and 14 ties; the tie criterion and meaning of the uncertainty notation are unspecified.
Specific finding: The concentration of a first-letter classifier's probe projection in a single SAE feature provides a useful operational diagnostic of feature splitting or absorption.

Specific finding: First-letter absorption can be screened using latent contributions along a supervised probe direction, extending the diagnostic to layers where source-token ablations no longer affect first-letter prediction.

Specific finding: First-letter absorption can be screened using latent contributions along a supervised probe direction, extending the diagnostic to layers where source-token ablations no longer affect first-letter prediction.

Specific finding: A meta-SAE can approximately decompose selected language-model SAE decoder directions into sparse components with human-recognizable semantic and lexical interpretations. Trained a BatchTopK k=4 meta-SAE on 49,152 decoder directions for 2,000 batches of size 16,384. Selected examples include Einstein, rugby, Android, and phrase-related latents. Components were interpreted through their strongly activating SAE latents and associated examples. Some examples are explicitly cherry-picked, and the most frequent meta-latent lacks a clear interpretation.
location: Defining Meta-SAEs; Meta-latents form interpretable decompositions of SAE latents; Are Meta-Latents different from SAE Latents?

experiment_summary: Specific finding: Understanding a manageable set of primitive features and their construction rules may permit useful mechanistic understanding without enumerating every constructed feature.

Specific finding: SAE representations can make labeled concepts readily recoverable and individual features predictively specialized while distributing each concept across multiple features. Section 4.2 reports high DCI disentanglement, informativeness, and explicitness alongside low completeness across evaluated SAE architectures and correlation conditions. This supports accessible but distributed concept information. Finite scores short of their theoretical optima do not establish population identifiability.
Specific finding: Combining several SAE coordinates can improve recovery of simple labeled concepts over using one coordinate, with saturation depending on architecture. Sparse probes on Top-K, SpADE, sparse shift, and natural-language SAE features generally approach saturation around ten coordinates. Appendix E reports that ReLU does not begin saturating over the examined 10–50-feature range. Top-K and sparse shift representations show favorable MCC–sparsity tradeoffs; the native-coordinate comparison is less favorable in Pythia than in Gemma.
Specific finding: Feature splitting may distribute antibody gene-identity information across correlated residue-level SAE latents, limiting reliable control through individual predictive latents.

Specific finding: Feature splitting and reconstruction-oriented SAE training objectives may fragment abstract answerability information into specialized coordinates that transfer poorly across domains.

Specific finding: Increasing prompted Big Five trait levels can increase corresponding personality ratings of LLM-generated social media text under a human-trained personality scorer. For each model and targeted trait, compares nine instructed levels across 50 biographies, yielding 450 profiles per correlation. All 20 reported Spearman correlations are positive, ranging from 0.47 for Flan-PaLM openness to 0.89 for GPT-4o agreeableness; all are reported at p < 0.0001. Mean correlations per model range from 0.68 to 0.82. These outcomes concern scorer-rated expression under explicit prompting, without independent human evaluation of the synthetic text.

Specific finding: Personality portrait prompts can change human-perceived Big Five expression in text-davinci-003's responses to selected hypothetical scenarios, with effectiveness varying by trait and direction. One hundred valid participants were divided into 50 evaluating P² and 50 evaluating searched-word prompts; each completed ten binary comparisons against neutral responses. Reported P² positive/negative success rates are openness 0.77/0.90, conscientiousness 0.73/0.45, extraversion 0.90/0.92, agreeableness 0.88/0.84, and neuroticism 0.68/0.74. P² exceeds the word baseline in nine of ten conditions, with positive agreeableness the exception. Negative conscientiousness remains below 0.5. Uncertainty estimates and the precise aggregation underlying the reported proportions are not supplied.

Specific finding: Personality-conditioned GPT narratives exhibit trait-associated LIWC patterns that partly overlap human essay associations, with the relative alignment of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 depending on the trait. Point-biserial analyses report shared significant LIWC features relative to the human-significant feature sets. GPT-3.5 versus GPT-4 counts are 16/18 versus 10/18 for extraversion, 16/23 versus 13/23 for agreeableness, 1/31 versus 11/31 for conscientiousness, 7/27 versus 15/27 for neuroticism, and 2/36 versus 17/36 for openness. Representative shared patterns include positive tone for extraversion, reduced conflict for agreeableness, and curiosity for openness. The source does not describe a multiple-comparison correction. Appendix G supplies additional BFI-score correlations but contains discrepancies between several verbal interpretations and printed signs.
Specific finding: BFI self-report scores of prompted GPT-4 personas can correlate with human personality ratings of their narratives, with the strongest correspondence for extraversion. Uninformed human ratings have reported Spearman correlations of .64, .33, .26, .23, and .22 with persona BFI scores for extraversion through openness. The first three have reported p < .001 and the last two p < .005. Informed-condition correlations are .42 and .32 for extraversion and agreeableness, both p < .001, and .20 and .17 for conscientiousness and neuroticism, both p < .05; openness is nonsignificant. The supplied text does not clearly specify how repeated ratings enter the significance calculations or report a direct test of differences between condition-specific correlations.

Specific finding: Changes in preceding conversation, questionnaire format, and music-genre context can alter ChatGPT's IPIP personality-trait scores without explicit personality instructions. Figure 13 reports ANOVA-detected IPIP effects for simulated conversations, textual formats, and Wikipedia paragraphs, described as less pronounced than PVQ/VSM effects. Nonsignificant trait conditions are indicated by figure shading unavailable in the supplied rendering, so exact trait-specific outcomes and plotted magnitudes cannot be recovered.
Specific finding: Ongoing conversation can revise an LLM dialogue agent's initially prompted persona and elicit roles different from those intended by its designers.

Specific finding: Narrative and conversational patterns learned during language-model pretraining provide a repertoire of character archetypes that can be elicited and refined through dialogue context.

Specific finding: Human behavioral regularities encoded during language-model training provide useful priors for generating plausible character actions and dialogue when conditioned on identities, situations, and histories.

Specific finding: Adding access to observations, stored plans, and reflections in a nested sequence can improve human-rated believability of language-model agent interview responses. One hundred evaluators ranked five conditions on one question from each of five interview categories. Architectural TrueSkill means increased from 21.21 without memory access to 25.64 with observations, 26.88 with observations and plans, and 29.89 with all three memory types. The paper reports Holm-adjusted Dunn pairwise p<0.001 between the architectural conditions. The reported Kruskal–Wallis and Dunn analyses do not explicitly account for the within-subject dependence.
Specific finding: A memory-, reflection-, and planning-equipped language-model agent can receive higher interview-believability rankings than a basic crowdworker roleplay baseline with access to the same character history. In the 100-evaluator within-subject comparison, the full architecture obtained TrueSkill mean 29.89 versus 22.95 for crowdworkers, with reported Holm-adjusted Dunn p<0.001. A distinct worker authored each agent's responses after inspecting its replay and memories; four response sets were replaced after basic quality screening. The reported inferential analysis does not explicitly model repeated judgments within evaluators.

Specific finding: Interacting language-model agents with external memories can spread initially private seeded information through their generated conversations. Reported knowledge of Sam's candidacy increased from 1/25 to 8/25 agents and knowledge of Isabella's party from 1/25 to 13/25. End-of-run interviews were labeled for awareness, and affirmative reports were checked against source dialogue in memory streams. No affirmative awareness report for these two topics was found hallucinated.
Specific finding: Repeated interaction among memory-equipped language-model agents can increase mutual acquaintance as measured by interviews checked against recorded experiences. Beginning- and end-of-run interviews defined an undirected edge when two agents knew of each other, with affirmative answers checked against memory streams. Reported network density increased from 0.167 to 0.74. Six of 453 awareness responses were identified as hallucinated; the text does not fully explain this response denominator relative to the possible directed agent pairs or specify their treatment in the graph.
Specific finding: Seeding an event-organizing intention in one language-model agent can lead to invitations, preparation, and coordinated attendance by other agents without individually scripting those behaviors. Specific finding: Sparse random re-encoding followed by piecewise-linear rounding can restore low-interference encodings of sparse Boolean states. experiment_summary: Specific finding: Language models compute more distinct meaningful input features than they have MLP neurons available to represent those features separately.

Specific finding: Boolean-task MLPs can learn overlapping, polysemantic feature codes even when enough hidden neurons are available to assign each target clause a separate neuron. The described learned weights of a 16-input, 16-hidden-neuron network trained on eight disjoint pairwise-AND clauses show multiple clauses sharing individual neurons. The representative run uses 30,000 balanced examples and 2,000 Adam-training epochs. A clause-per-neuron implementation fits within the available width. The proposed explanation involving more numerous overlapping-code local minima is not tested.
Specific finding: Gradient-trained ReLU MLPs solving controlled Boolean tasks can develop overlapping neuron codes that bring a clause's inputs together for soft Boolean computation. Weight inspection, clause-associated sign-pattern counts, matched random-matrix comparisons, and selected execution traces identify repeated coding structures. Positive four-literal clauses exhibit enriched 4P patterns in positive-witness rows; clauses with one negated literal exhibit enriched 3P1N patterns aligned with that literal. Most Section 4 statistics analyze matrices composed with a known Hadamard input embedding. The evidence does not include comprehensive interventions validating every inferred channel.

experiment_summary: Specific finding: Neuron-level circuits are messy because features are stored in superposition and MLPs compute on those features in superposition, performing more than one computation per neuron.

Specific finding: APD can learn parameter components that approximately recover coordinate-specific computations distributed across two residual MLP layers. Starting from 200 parameter components, APD produces components whose neuron-contribution patterns approximately match individual input computations across both layers. Recovery is less clean than in the one-layer case: more components mix two feature computations, and some features require several components. Appendix C.4 reports improved separation under per-layer rank-one constraints without tabulated aggregate effect sizes.
Specific finding: APD can approximately separate coordinate-specific nonlinear computations that share neurons in a residual MLP with fewer neurons than target coordinate functions. APD starts with 130 components on independently sparse inputs with activation probability 0.01 and uniform nonzero values in [-1,1]. Comparisons of target and component neuron-contribution patterns show approximate feature-specific recovery using the same neurons. Output-MSE analyses reveal shrinkage, secondary feature contributions, and features requiring multiple components. Numerical aggregate recovery scores are not tabulated, and the target itself only approximately implements the coordinate functions.

Specific finding: Stochastic Parameter Decomposition can isolate feature-specific input-weight subcomponents whose neuron-contribution patterns closely match those of a residual MLP computing more feature-specific ReLU functions than it has neurons. SPD finds 100 input-matrix subcomponents corresponding to the 100 input dimensions. The text and captions for Figures 6–7 report close agreement between target and decomposed weight-derived contributions across all 100 features and 50 neurons. At a suitable importance penalty, one-hot inputs of magnitude 0.75 select their corresponding input subcomponent. No aggregate numerical contribution-error statistic is supplied.
Specific finding: Stochastic Parameter Decomposition can recover feature-column directions in small superposition reconstruction models with little average matched-column norm distortion. Table 1 reports MMCS rounding to 1.000 ± 0.000 for all four configurations. Mean L2 ratios are 0.993 ± 0.002 for TMS5-2, 1.010 ± 0.007 for TMS40-10, 0.992 ± 0.010 for TMS5-2+ID, and 1.031 ± 0.001 for TMS40-10+ID. These measure best-matched column direction and average magnitude, rather than exhaustive behavioral or mechanistic fidelity. The run count underlying the reported standard deviations is unspecified. APD norm ratios near 0.9 are attributed to Braun et al. (2025), not a documented matched rerun here.
Specific finding: Stochastic Parameter Decomposition can recover feature-associated input-weight subcomponents across multiple residual MLP blocks with neuron-contribution patterns resembling the original network's distributed computations. Learned importance patterns associate input-matrix subcomponents in different blocks with individual features. The two-block comparison has systematic contribution inflation of unknown origin, and the authors report seed sensitivity for these models. Specific finding: SPD can obtain structured decompositions of hidden-identity superposition models and three-block compressed-computation models that were reported as unsuccessful or impractically difficult for APD. Comparisons on previously studied models reference Braun et al. (2025). The new evidence establishes SPD feasibility on these examples more directly than comparative scalability or tuning robustness.

experiment_summary:
Specific finding: Representing every ordering of a fixed set of m' distinct pairwise AND operations requires worst-case Ω(m' log m') parameter-description bits, even when a fixed error fraction below one half is allowed on the corresponding m' two-hot inputs. Formal reduction in Corollaries A.2.1–A.2.2: a greedy permutation-code construction supplies a separated family with logarithmic cardinality Ω(m' log m'). Ordered AND outputs on the selected two-hot inputs implement permutations of one-hot labels. Unique decoding and counting yield the asymptotic worst-case description bound, subject to rounding and separation conventions rather than the source's exact almost-all formulation.
Specific finding: A fixed architecture exactly computing every unordered collection of m' distinct pairwise ANDs requires worst-case parameter-description capacity of order log binomial(binomial(m,2),m'). Formal counting argument in Corollary A.2.3: different subsets of AND pairs yield different output multisets on a two-hot input corresponding to a pair in their symmetric difference. Consequently, the architecture needs at least binomial(binomial(m,2),m') distinguishable parameter settings. This establishes the asymptotic worst-case description bound, with the same qualification about exact almost-all variable-length thresholds.
Specific finding: Constant-depth square-width networks with constant bits per parameter need width Ω(√(m' log m')) to express every ordered m'-output AND instance on the specified sparse input sets. Formal resource-counting derivation: combine the Ω(m' log m') description-bit requirement with O(dn²) affine-network parameters and bounded description length per parameter. Constant depth is necessary for the stated width-only consequence; Section 2.2 otherwise permits arbitrary depth.
location: Section 4, Corollaries 4.2.1–4.2.2; Appendix A.1, Corollaries A.2.1–A.2.2

experiment_summary: Specific finding: A fixed architecture approximating all unordered collections of m' distinct pairwise ANDs requires worst-case Ω(m') parameter-description bits on a suitable selected two-hot input set when the error fraction is a fixed constant below 1/8. Appendix A.3 gives a formal proof attempt using subsets of size m' from 2m' candidate pairs, represented by fixed-weight binary codewords. The intended distance is at least m'/2, giving input disagreement at least 1/4. The code-size justification needs a fixed-weight argument, so the complete claimed result is not treated as established evidence here.
Specific finding: The finite-bit description of a network implementing independently specified operations must contain enough information to specify their joint computational content.

experiment_summary:
Specific finding: Known feature axes in compressed denoising networks can have plateau-boundary exponents above two that decline toward two as perturbations become misaligned with those axes. Optimizes denoising parameters using Gaussian-corrupted two-hot inputs, then performs deterministic additive perturbations without perturbation-time noise. Each fit uses 60 mixing angles and a 2,500-point magnitude scan on [0,25], with a per-network threshold based on feature axis e2. Ground-truth axes yield aggregate p approximately 3–3.4 across the three feature-to-neuron ratios; interpolation toward random vectors reduces p toward two. One d=8,192 contour has p=2.91 and 0.13% mean radial residual. Appendix C.2's displayed expression for y omits the decoder, although its subsequent definition of f and loss include it; the perturbation criterion is written using f.
Specific finding: MELBO directions and selected frequently active SAE decoder directions in Gemma-2-9B can exhibit plateau-boundary exponents above two. MELBO directions yield mean p=2.21, 95% direction-bootstrap CI [2.01, 2.42], median 2.16. Selected SAE directions yield mean p=2.28 [2.14, 2.47], median 2.19. These results concern the selected direction populations, rather than all SAE latents or a six-model comparison of these direction types.

experiment_summary:
Specific finding: Clause-aligned positive-witness codes can stabilize before a Boolean MLP achieves low training error, while subsequent changes in negative-witness patterns accompany the remaining improvement. Pattern trajectories averaged over ten runs show positive 4P prevalence increasing within the first epoch and stabilizing around epoch two, while substantial training error remains. Later negative-witness reorganization accompanies error removal. Section 4.6 inconsistently identifies some negative patterns as 3P1N versus 3N1P, so their exact identities cannot be cleanly resolved from the supplied prose.
Specific finding: In controlled four-literal DNF learning, increasing formula complexity can increase training error alongside declining clause-aligned code counts and increasing numbers of clauses without codes. Ten random-formula trials per configuration use 20,000 samples and up to 100 Adam-training epochs. The prose reports training-error onset around clause counts matching hidden width and average 4P counts below approximately 1.5–2 per clause. Missing-code counts also track error. A separate fixed-64-clause width sweep relates lower error to greater code prevalence and uses half the earlier training epochs. Most Section 4 statistics use known-Hadamard-composed weight matrices.
Specific finding: Shared hidden layers trained on multiple Boolean outputs can develop feature-code rows preferentially associated with particular outputs, alongside negative-witness rows. The two-output example trains on 50,000 inputs for 1,000 epochs and reaches 97.30% test accuracy with both bits correct. The three-output example uses 200,000 inputs for 1,000 epochs and reaches 95.05% with all three bits correct. The prose reports that sorting rows by their largest positive output weight reveals output-associated clause codes, less cleanly for three outputs. Initial four-output attempts have error rates around one third; their error denominator is not specified.
Specific finding: A small MLP trained on a conjunction of disjoint positive two-variable OR clauses can exhibit a channel structure consistent with detecting clause violations and negating their disjunction. The representative 16-hidden-neuron network is trained on 40,000 inputs with each variable independently true with probability 0.75. The prose describes negative-output-weight rows with codes interpreted as soft conjunctions of negated variable pairs, whose negative output contributions implement rejection of violated clauses. Other formulas are described as consistent, without quantitative mechanism-recovery results or a comprehensive intervention test.
Specific finding: Codes extracted from positive-witness weight signs can approximately recover the locations of consecutive-four binary patterns from hidden activations, despite training the network only for binary pattern detection. Across fifty training runs and 2,000 same-distribution test inputs per run, the positive-witness code decoder has mean false-positive and false-negative rates of 6.82% and 7.66%, with standard deviations 1.82% and 0.97%. The original network's corresponding rates are 0.71% and 1.65%, with standard deviations 0.33% and 0.37%. Exact recovery of the complete set of pattern locations, including empty sets for negative inputs, averages 82.63%, with standard deviation 1.80%.

experiment_summary: Specific finding: Activation differences between an original model and its fine-tuned derivative on a shared prompt provide sufficiently meaningful inputs for interpreting verbalizations as descriptions of fine-tuning-induced content.

Specific finding: Narrowly fine-tuned language models can exhibit objective-related vocabulary readouts from mean early-token activation differences computed on unrelated text. Patchscope readouts of mean differences are compared with readouts of mean original and fine-tuned activations. The text reports 20–80% relevance at selected positions and stronger readouts than Logit Lens. Alternative token graders preserve the qualitative advantage of difference vectors, despite systematic relevance differences and nominal Krippendorff alpha of 0.65. The subliminal condition consists of one selected model with reliable cat preference.
Specific finding: Activation differences against a pretrained reference can retain readable traces of subsequent narrow synthetic-document fine-tuning even when they also include the intervening base-to-chat transformation. Agents retain objective-identification ability using pretrained-to-fine-tuned-chat differences. The authors report no significant grade difference between reference choices, despite weaker trace metrics with the pretrained reference. The supplied text provides no numerical equivalence test or effect-size bound.
Specific finding: Positionwise mean differences between original and fine-tuned residual activations on unrelated text can be interpreted through calibrated vocabulary readouts and additive steering. The method is evaluated on 33 narrow organisms using decoded-token relevance, steered-output embedding similarity, and agent objective-recovery grades. Patchscope combines three identity prompts and selects a scale from a supplied grid; steering uses norm-normalized vectors and a coherence-based search.
Specific finding: Adding mean early-token checkpoint-difference vectors during generation can increase semantic similarity between unrelated-prompt responses and the model's narrow fine-tuning data. Five generations per prompt at temperature 1.1 are compared with 500 fine-tuning examples, ordinary generations, and 500 Tulu chat examples. For chat-format datasets, comparisons use assistant responses. Difference-vector steering produces higher reported similarity to fine-tuning data. Alternative coherence graders yield highly correlated selected strengths and retain the qualitative similarity result.
Specific finding: Replacing LoRA with full fine-tuning does not eliminate readable ADL traces under the tested narrow SDF recipes. Retrained full-fine-tuning models retain clearly detectable token and steering biases, described as slightly stronger than LoRA biases. In fully fine-tuned Gemma3-1B, relevant tokens can also be decoded from mean fine-tuned activations alone. Numerical effect sizes and repeated-training variability are not supplied in the readable prose.
Specific finding: Training-time removal of the span of five previously extracted middle-layer ADL directions can leave substantial readable SDF traces. During fine-tuning, the projection onto the span of the first five extracted difference vectors is subtracted at the middle layer, affecting forward and backward computation. The authors report modest bias reduction with substantial remaining bias across all three models; they describe agent-grade evidence of improvement in only one model condition.
Specific finding: The readability and steering effectiveness of SDF activation-difference traces depend on extraction position and layer, with different extraction choices favoring vocabulary readout and steering. Section 4.3 reports that informative positions vary by model and objective, later positions generally carry less information, and single-position agent performance becomes more variable later in the sequence. Appendix F.1 reports stronger token relevance at greater depth, especially the final layer, while steering performs best at the middle layer among the evaluated depths. Numerical curves are unavailable in the text rendering.

Specific finding: Adding unrelated C4 examples to a fixed SDF corpus can substantially reduce ADL trace readability while weakening implanted-fact learning by model-dependent amounts. experiment_summary: Specific finding: The tested broad chat-tuned checkpoints and domain-adapted vision-language models show weaker ADL signatures than the selected narrow model organisms. Chat-tuning token and steering scores show no clear advantage over baselines, apart from seven ambiguously relevant Chinese tokens at one Qwen position. Biomedical, food, and remote-sensing fine-tunes show small residual steering biases. ADL-only agents sometimes identify domain content and reportedly outperform the 50-query baseline, whereas agents with five extra text-only queries can become distracted and perform similarly to baselines.

Specific finding: Model organisms expressing approximately matched behavioral quirks can receive substantially different white-box interpretability scores under different construction recipes. Compared construction variants after tuning training exposure and learning rate toward family-specific integrated-DPO QER. For AO, steering, and logit lens, excluding variants below estimated noise floors, reported within-family highest-to-lowest score ratios span 1.2–20.4. Main scores select the best of two AO layers or three steering/logit-lens layers. MilitarySubmarine OLMo SDF variants are excluded from main analyses because black-box discovery is confounded. These comparisons establish recipe dependence without isolating objective alone.
Specific finding: Changing the reference checkpoint used for activation differences can substantially change measured quirk interpretability. Compared differences from the nearest common pre-DPO ancestor with differences from a separately reproduced vanilla-DPO sibling checkpoint. AO and steering scores are often, but not always, roughly similar; logit-lens scores diverge widely. Numerical effect sizes are not supplied in the text accompanying Figure 18.
Specific finding: Access to a reference model can improve activation-oracle and logit-lens quirk detection while changing the relative interpretability rankings of organism variants. Compared interpretation of organism–reference activation differences with interpretation of organism activations alone. Diffing performs better in the reported above-noise comparisons. ItalianFood AO scores are approximately constant across recipes without diffing but differ greatly with diffing. The comparison measures performance under these specific readout procedures rather than establishing that every auditing method benefits from a reference.

experiment_summary: Specific finding: Activation-oracle verbalizations of original-versus-fine-tuned activation differences can support harmful-fine-tuning-domain identification with reported mean audit scores comparable to Activation Difference Lens.
